See summary above for the short version. Full markdown report follows.

# Track 30 — Model-Agnostic Classifier Adapter Layer

**Verdict: PROTOTYPE FIRST | Novelty: Low-Moderate | Scope: CORE EXTENSION (InProcessInterface)**

## Summary

`InProcessInterface` should stay a single abstract contract — `predict(image) -> {race, gender, age}` (+ optional per-class probabilities) — but stop being FairFace-only. Two concrete adapters implement it: an **ONNX Runtime adapter** (format-agnostic, covers anything exported from PyTorch/TF/etc.) and a **HuggingFace `image-classification` pipeline adapter** (lower integration effort, narrower model coverage). Both sit on top of one shared, non-optional component — a **TaxonomyMapper** — because the actual hard problem isn't inference, it's reconciling a third-party model's own output space with the locked `race_7`/`gender_2`/`age_9` Literal (the "M1 lock" in schema.py). Neither adapter is useful without it, so it should not be built twice. Auditing a model whose native taxonomy has no faithful mapping onto M1 is explicitly out of scope for this track — that's Track 23's problem, and coordination note below flags that Track 23 is currently marked *dropped* in team memory while this task's own spec still names it as the prerequisite.

---

## 1. Problem framing

- `PredictionsFileInterface` (CSV/JSON ingestion) never faces this problem: the file already contains labels in the project's fixed taxonomy, because whoever produced it did the mapping out-of-band.
- `InProcessInterface` runs a model live and must produce those same fixed labels itself. FairFace ResNet-34 is trivial because it was trained to natively output exactly `race_7`/`gender_2`/`age_9`. A third-party model was not. It may:
  - use a different number of classes per task (a 5-way race head, a binary vs. 9-bucket age head),
  - use different class *semantics* even at the same cardinality (age buckets with different bin edges),
  - expose only 1-2 of the 3 tasks (a gender-only classifier),
  - not be organized into these 3 tasks at all (a general ImageNet classifier — out of scope, see §5).
- Consequence: **adapters cannot output the fixed taxonomy directly from model output**. Every adapter needs a mapping step between "model's native label" and "project's locked label," supplied by whoever registers the model, not inferred automatically.

## 2. Shared component: `TaxonomyMapper` (build this once, both adapters depend on it)

Config-driven, not code-driven — one mapping artifact per registered third-party model:

```yaml
# example: client_model_mapping.yaml
model_id: acme-face-classifier-v3
tasks:
  race:
    source_labels: [white, black, asian, other]        # this model's own 4 classes
    mapping:
      white: White
      black: Black
      asian: East Asian          # collapses model's "asian" into one of FairFace's 7
      other: null                # null = unmapped -> policy below
    unmapped_policy: exclude_from_race_metrics   # reject | exclude_from_race_metrics | collapse_to_other
  gender:
    source_labels: [male, female]
    mapping: {male: Male, female: Female}
    unmapped_policy: reject       # gender_2 is exhaustive here, no excuse for a miss
  age:
    source_labels: null           # model doesn't expose age at all
    mapping: null                 # -> age task simply not eligible for this model
```

Validation at adapter **construction time** (fail fast, not at audit time on record 40,000):
1. Every `source_label` the model can actually emit is either mapped or has an explicit `unmapped_policy`. No silent drops.
2. Every mapped *target* is a member of the locked `race_7`/`gender_2`/`age_9` Literal — reuse the same validator `schema.py` already uses for `PredictionsFileInterface` rows, don't write a second one.
3. A task with `source_labels: null` marks that task **ineligible** for this model — it must flow into `eligible_groups()` (base.py, per Track 29's finding) the same way a missing column does today for file-based input, not throw.
4. `unmapped_policy: reject` at construction means "this model cannot be audited on this task as configured" — surfaced to the user as a config error, not a runtime crash mid-audit.

This mapper is a plain Python object (`{task: {source_label: target_label | None}}` plus a policy enum) — both adapters call `TaxonomyMapper.resolve(task, raw_output)` after their own model-specific inference step. It has zero ONNX or HF dependency, so it is trivially unit-testable against a canned raw-output fixture and reusable by any future adapter (e.g. a hypothetical REST-API adapter later).

### Collapsing classes changes calibration — flag, don't solve here

When several source classes collapse into one target class (the `asian → East Asian` line above), the adapter has to decide how to combine their probabilities: **sum** (correct under a partition — the true probability of "East Asian" is the probability mass across every source class mapped to it) is the recommended default over **max** (which understates true confidence and breaks calibration-sensitive metrics). This is a probability-semantics decision, not an implementation detail, and it should be validated empirically once a real collapsed-taxonomy model is on hand — flagging as a follow-on rather than solving speculatively here.

## 3. Adapter A — ONNX Runtime (`ONNXRuntimeAdapter`)

Model-format-agnostic: anything exported to `.onnx` from PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, etc. is coverable, which is the actual value of this adapter over HF's.

**What it needs to be built, concretely** (confirmed against `onnxruntime`'s actual API surface):
- `onnxruntime.InferenceSession(model_path, providers=[...])` — session construction is the only "load" step; there is no `AutoImageProcessor` equivalent bundled in.
- **Preprocessing is 100% the integrator's responsibility.** ONNX carries no image-processing metadata — resize dims, channel order, mean/std normalization, NCHW vs NHWC all have to be supplied per model (typically alongside the mapping YAML in §2) and applied before `session.run()`.
- **Output is a bare `(1, num_classes)` logit/probability array per task**, addressed by output tensor name (`session.get_outputs()[i].name`) — no label strings, no id2label. This is the concrete form of the "hard part" named in the task spec: the adapter must apply softmax (if raw logits) and then index into `source_labels` positionally (`source_labels[argmax_index]`) before it can even call `TaxonomyMapper.resolve()`. If the integrator's declared `source_labels` order doesn't match the model's actual output column order, failures are silent and wrong, not crashes — this ordering must be treated as a validated, versioned part of the mapping config, not folklore.
- Multi-task models (single ONNX graph with 3 output heads for race/gender/age) vs. multi-model (3 separate `.onnx` files) both need supporting — the adapter should accept 1-3 `InferenceSession`s keyed by task, not assume one session = one task.

**Effort:** highest of the two — integrator supplies preprocessing spec + positional label order + mapping YAML. Full control over batching/execution provider (CPU/CUDA), which matters for large-scale audits (tens of thousands of images).

## 4. Adapter B — HuggingFace `image-classification` pipeline (`HFPipelineAdapter`)

Lower-effort alternative, narrower coverage (models published on the Hub with an `AutoModelForImageClassification`-compatible config).

**What it needs to be built, concretely** (confirmed against `transformers` pipeline source):
- `pipeline("image-classification", model=model_id)` handles image preprocessing internally (via the model's paired `AutoImageProcessor`) — the adapter does **not** need a separate preprocessing spec, which is the main effort saving over the ONNX path.
- Output is `[{"label": <string>, "score": <float>}, ...]`, where the label string comes from the model's own `config.id2label` — **already a human-readable string, not a bare index.** This makes the `TaxonomyMapper` config easier to author correctly (`"Black": "Black"` is auditable at a glance; `3: "Black"` is not) and removes the ONNX adapter's silent-reordering failure mode entirely.
- `top_k` defaults to 5 and is capped at `model.config.num_labels` — for a full-distribution read (needed for the sum-based collapse in §2), request `top_k=model.config.num_labels` (i.e. all classes), not the pipeline default.
- Same multi-task gap as ONNX: a single HF pipeline produces one flat label list. A model doing all of race/gender/age in one head needs its combined labels (e.g. `"young_asian_male"`) parsed into three sub-mappings; a model with 3 separate task-specific pipelines needs 3 `HFPipelineAdapter` instances composed under one `InProcessInterface` — same composition pattern as multi-session ONNX.

**Effort:** lower — no manual preprocessing spec, string labels reduce mapping-authoring errors. Trade-off: restricted to models that fit the `AutoModelForImageClassification` pattern, and per-call Python-level pipeline overhead is worse than a raw ONNX session at audit-scale batch throughput — acceptable for prototyping/smaller audits, worth re-benchmarking before recommending it for a production high-volume audit path.

## 5. Explicitly out of scope

Auditing a model whose **native demographic taxonomy has no faithful mapping onto the locked `race_7`/`gender_2`/`age_9` space** — e.g. a client model that only distinguishes "adult/minor" instead of `age_9`'s buckets, or uses a racial/ethnic categorization scheme with no natural collapse or expansion onto FairFace's 7 categories — is **not** solvable by adapters alone. `TaxonomyMapper`'s `unmapped_policy` can only drop or exclude individual stray classes; it cannot repair a *structurally* incompatible taxonomy without either (a) fabricating a mapping that corrupts the resulting bias metrics, or (b) BiasAperture supporting more than one demographic schema at the schema layer. That's Track 23 (cross-modal schema generalization), not this track. This adapter layer's contract is: **if a faithful mapping exists, these adapters can serve it; if it doesn't, that's a Track 23 problem, not an adapter problem.** Don't conflate the two by trying to make an adapter "smart" about incompatible taxonomies.

**Coordination flag:** Track 29's memory entry (2026-09-02) marks Track 23 as **"(dropped)"**, while this task's own spec still names Track 23 cross-modal schema work as the explicit prerequisite for out-of-scope cases. Surfacing the discrepancy rather than resolving it — whoever owns the Phase-2 board should confirm whether Track 23 is dropped (in which case genuinely incompatible-taxonomy models are simply unsupported for the foreseeable future, not deferred) or was dropped-then-reopened.

## 6. Recommendation

- Build `TaxonomyMapper` first, as a standalone unit — it's the load-bearing piece, has no ML framework dependency, and both adapters are thin wrappers around "run inference, get raw labels, call the mapper."
- Prototype the **HF pipeline adapter** before the ONNX adapter: lower effort, string-keyed labels reduce the highest-risk failure mode (silent positional mis-mapping), good enough to validate the whole `InProcessInterface` + `TaxonomyMapper` contract end-to-end.
- Layer the **ONNX adapter** in second, once the contract is proven, since it's where real client-supplied production models will actually land (Hub-hosted HF models are a minority of what a client will hand over).
- Do not build model-format support beyond these two without a concrete named model in hand — this track scopes designs, not a plugin marketplace.
